chunks: From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Sandal, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves from among His believing servants every servant who supplicates. Therefore, it is upon you to supplicate during the pre-dawn period until the emergence of the sun, for it is a time in which the doors of the sky are opened, sustenance is distributed, and great needs are fulfilled.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of supplicating during the pre-dawn hours in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the spiritual act of dua to the cosmic mechanics of rizq (sustenance) and divine favor. This period, known as the 'time of acceptance,' is historically emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as a critical window for istighathah (seeking help), reflecting the belief that divine decree is actively distributed during these hours.
